title: Refactor continuous queue allocator and KV priming pipeline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We have accumulated several small hacks in the continuous batching path and the KV prefix priming logic that together cause tail latency spikes and unpredictable memory churn under bursty workloads. This ticket refactors the queue allocation interface (the component that maps incoming requests to in-flight batch lanes), replaces ad-hoc soft-reservations with a clearer time-sliced reservation window, and extracts KV priming into a standalone pipeline with clearer failure semantics and backpressure. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 latency variance, simplify reasoning about hot-key behavior, and remove ongoing synchronization contention that blocks other scheduler initiatives.
technical_approach: Introduce a Continuous Queue Allocator abstraction that exposes: try_reserve(queue_id, deadline), release_reservation(id), and promote_to_commit(id). This is a narrower API than the current slot allocator and avoids external locking across the batch controller.
Split KV priming (prefetch of KV entries) into a separate bounded worker pool with explicit lease tokens so priming work never starves allocator threads.
Migrate existing soft-reservations to time-sliced reservations (configurable slice_ms) so long-running tokens are preemptable and we avoid head-of-line blocking.
Replace a global atomic counter used for lane allocation with per-shard token buckets to reduce cross-thread contention under multi-socket hosts.
Add careful metrics and tracing points for reservation lifecycle, priming queue depth, prefetch hit/miss, and per-request stall time for root-cause analysis.

Run dependency upgrades in parallel: bump grpc to 1.57.x to pick up improved I/O scheduling, and upgrade the internal ringbuffer lib used by the allocator to v2.1 which exposes non-blocking pop semantics.
Add unit tests for reservation fairness and integration load tests with synthetic hot-key and burst patterns.
Provide a migration toggle (runtime flag) to switch to the new allocator and priming pipeline with canary rollout at the pod level.
Document fallback behavior: if priming worker pool is saturated, requests should fall back to on-demand KV fetch with metrics recording and per-request timeout to avoid indefinite stalls.
Coordinate with autoscaler team to ensure changes do not violate current autoscaling invariants.
Benchmarks: target 8-12% p99 improvement on typical LLM chat workload with 4k sequence and 50 concurrent clients; aim for reduced CPU jitter under burst traffic.

acceptance_criteria: Allocator API implemented and covered by unit tests (>=90% branch coverage for new files)
KV priming path isolated behind worker pool with clear backpressure behavior
Benchmark shows at least 8% reduction in p99 latency vs baseline on standard chat bench
No increase in error-rate or request timeouts after canary at 10% traffic for 48h
All relevant metrics emitted (reservation_acquired, reservation_preempted, priming_queue_depth, priming_worker_utilization)
Feature flag allows immediate rollback without pod restarts
Code reviewed and approved by two senior runtime engineers and one performance PM
Dependencies upgraded and CI green on linux-amd64 and linux-arm64 builds
notes: We intentionally keep the allocator API minimal to reduce coupling with the batch controller; future work can extend promotion semantics for multi-hop aggregation.
Trade-off: introducing a priming worker pool adds another moving part but simplifies retry semantics for KV fetches and enables independent autoscaling in follow-ups.
Risk: grpc upgrade may expose subtle connection pooling behavior differences; plan includes a short soak test on staging.
This ticket avoids changing higher-level request coalescing heuristics (left for a follow-up) so we can land incremental improvements quickly.
Coordinate with release engineering for a migration window and post-deploy verification dashboard.
If p99 targets are not met, fallback plan is to revert preemption and iterate on token bucket sizes and slice_ms parameters.
decisions: Use time-sliced preemption vs strict lease TTLs to allow flexible preemption without full lease churn.
Keep KV priming out-of-path from allocator threads to bound tail latency impact.
Adopt per-shard token buckets to reduce cross-CPU synchronization even though it complicates fairness analysis slightly.
Upgrade grpc and ringbuffer now to avoid chasing backcompat issues later; tests will gate the change.
